CLIMATE NOTE

NOTE
Yesterday's high temperatures reached into the mid 60s across most areas (3 degrees from reaching the daily record high at Detroit). High temperatures should be just as warm today as a renewed surge of warm advection arrives with a 500 mb ridge axis translating through during the day. Strengthening low-level southwest flow as we head into Saturday supports even warmer temps, as 925 mb temps reach 14C, suggestive of highs near 70 degrees. This would lead to daily record high temperatures being broken (see climate section). However, the surface flow may remain backed enough out of the south- southeast to exert some cooler marine influence, particularly across Wayne County, and thus NBM temps are only suggesting highs in the lower 60s for the Detroit Metro Area. A pattern change and colder temperatures are on track to arrive early next week, as the 500 mb low over northern Alberta sinks south into the Dakotas on Sunday. Models differ on the interaction and speed of the upper-level trough over the Great Basin ejecting to the east. Sunday has a good shot of getting into the 60s once again if the slower cold front timing of the Canadian/GFS solutions verifies. A healthy moisture axis for late November standards (PW values up to 1 inch) arrives late in the afternoon into early evening. There looks to be sufficient forcing and frontogenesis with the front to support a line of showers. Aggressive drying arrives by midnight, however, as an extremely dry Arctic air mass (PW values of 0.1 to 0.25 inches) swings through the Great Lakes region Monday into Tuesday. Nonetheless, a seasonably cold air mass with 850 mb temps lowering into the -10 to -12 C range looks to support isolated to scattered light snow showers and flurries, predominantly Monday evening and night, as soundings indicate saturation briefly within the DGZ. An upper-level ridge quickly building in on Tuesday, per model consensus, will squash any lake-effect activity, even as 850 mb temps only slowly moderate. && .MARINE... As low pressure continues to lift northeast away from the region, surface high pressure continues to build in from the Mid Atlantic and upper level ridging builds in from the west. This will lead to above normal temperatures holding through the weekend. As the upper level trough approaches the region Saturday, winds will start to increase but stable conditions will limit gust potential. A cold front then dropping through the region Sunday night leading to stronger northwesterly flow and a cold air advection pushing across the lakes. There will be potential for headlines Sunday night into the new week with the increasing winds. && .CLIMATE... Record high max temperatures for November 20nd: Detroit: 70 Degrees (Set in 1942) Flint: 68 Degrees (Set in 1953) Saginaw: 69 Degrees (Set in 1931) Record high max temperatures for November 21st: Detroit: 67 Degrees (Set in 1913) Flint: 66 Degrees (Set in 1931) Saginaw: 69 Degrees (Set in 1913) Record high max temperatures for November 22nd: Detroit: 69 Degrees (Set in 1913) Flint: 65 Degrees (Set in 1934) Saginaw: 66 Degrees (Set in 1913) && .PREV DISCUSSION... Issued at 1141 PM EST Thu Nov 19 2026 AVIATION... Area surface observations indicate convergent flow off Lake Michigan into the KGRR area. The HRRR and RRFS solutions remain supportive of the idea of fog development within surface moisture convergence overnight, with the west-southwesterly wind component causing an eastward expansion of the fog layer into KFNT and possibly KPTK in the 12 to 14Z time frame. In light of this, morning fog has been ramped up in the KFNT TAF. There remains uncertainty as to the extent to which the fog may reach KPTK. Otherwise, the large scale high pressure system will maintain clear skies below 15k feet and light winds through the TAF period. For DTW...The chances for any early morning fog are forecast to remain northwest of DTW, with the probabilities of fog at the airport too low to include in the terminal at this time.
